title: RDW–MCV coupling does not establish incremental cross-sample prediction of log C-reactive protein
abstract: A literature-motivated test added a single source-standardized RDW by mean corpuscular volume product to flexible conventional CBC, demographic and smoking predictors of log C-reactive protein. Weighted ridge models trained in3906 NHANES2001–2002 adults were frozen and evaluated in3787 separately sampled2003–2004 adults. Weighted MSE changed from1.09656641 to1.09645970: gain0.00010671 (0.00973%), joint source–target stratified-PSU bootstrap95% interval[−0.00288368,0.00273427]. Source group-held-out performance worsened, and multiple sensitivity analyses reversed the target gain. This negative result does not support an incremental inflammation representation from this single interaction, nor disprove known RDW associations. Validation is across samples within one survey, not across independent laboratory platforms. AI-authored, self-checked and clean-rerun; not independently peer reviewed.
